## Responses and Adaptations of Hormones

Endocrine hormones are produced within glands, released into the blood, and then transported to target tissues where they bind to receptors either on the sarcolemma or in the sarcoplasm. provides a summary of the primary anabolic hormones and their actions. There is clear and compelling evidence that basal concentrations of anabolic hormones influence growth and regenerative capacity of skeletal muscle (46); when anabolic hormonal concentrations are chronically suppressed, muscular adaptations are blunted. The following sections address the hypertrophic role of the primary anabolic hormones (insulin-like growth factor 1, growth hormone, testosterone, and insulin) and the resistance training-mediated alterations caused by these hormones.
